title: Training Note — Billing the Hours of Controls Tickets Closed with No Fault Found
content:
# Training Note — Billing the Hours of Controls Tickets Closed with No Fault Found

**How much of the no-fault-found time is billed under the Building Automation Service Plans?** Where the tier includes a remote fix attempt and the twelve months to the handling day carry two or more tickets closed with no fault found, none of the hours logged on tickets closed with no fault found is billed. Where the tier includes a remote fix attempt and the twelve months to the handling day carry exactly one ticket closed with no fault found, half of those hours — 50 per cent of them — is billed. In every other case all of the hours logged on tickets closed with no fault found are billed.

| Tier includes a remote fix attempt | Tickets closed with no fault found in the twelve months to the handling day | Share of those hours billed |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 2 or more | none of them |
| yes | exactly 1 | half of them, that is 50 per cent |
| no | any number | all of them |

**Does the count include tickets closed some other way?** No: the count is of tickets closed with no fault found in the twelve months to the handling day, and only of those.

**What happens at a tier that includes no remote fix attempt?** All of the hours logged on tickets closed with no fault found are billed, whatever the count of such tickets.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** A plan whose tier includes a remote fix attempt shows one ticket closed with no fault found in the twelve months, carrying 3 hours. Half of those hours, that is 1.5 hours, is billed. Had there been two such tickets carrying 3 hours between them, none of the 3 hours would be billed.
